cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend: Jacob, Joseph's father, and his whole family are living in Egypt now, in the region of Goshen. God renamed Jacob Israel back in Genesis 32:28, so the text calls him both, and it calls his family the Israelites. Let's see how this family does in Goshen.

cards.question: The Israelites are settled in Goshen. How do they do there?

answers.text: They gain property and grow greatly in number
They lose their flocks and scatter across Egypt
They pack up and head back to Canaan

cards.question: True or false: Jacob lives in Egypt seventeen years, and he lives to be 147 years old.

cards.text: ONE HUNDRED FORTY-SEVEN, friend! I spent years in a junk drawer and thought THAT was a long time. Now the time draws near for Israel to die, and he calls Joseph in with a request about where he'll be buried.

cards.question: Jacob has Joseph put his hand under his thigh and promise to show him kindness and faithfulness. What is Jacob's request?

answers.text: Carry him out of Egypt to be buried with his fathers
Bury him right there in the land of Goshen
Bury him in Egypt wherever Joseph lives

cards.question: Joseph answers that he'll do as his father asked. True or false: Jacob takes his word for it and asks for nothing more.

cards.text: Jacob says, "Swear to me," and this man wants it SWORN, friend, no handshake deals. So Joseph swears.

cards.question: Once Joseph swears, Israel bows in ___ at the head of his bed.

cards.text: Some time later, Joseph gets word: "Your father is ill." So he sets out with his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.

cards.question: True or false: When Jacob is told that Joseph has come, he's too weak to even sit up.

cards.text: Israel rallies his strength and sits UP in bed, like me when the oven timer dings. Then he tells Joseph that God Almighty appeared to him at Luz, in the land of Canaan, and blessed him there.

cards.question: At Luz, God promised to make Jacob ___ and to give the land to his descendants after him.

cards.text: Now Jacob turns to Joseph's two boys, the ones born to Joseph in Egypt before Jacob came. And what he says about them is BIG, friend.

cards.question: What does Jacob say about Ephraim and Manasseh, Joseph's two boys born in Egypt?

answers.text: They will be counted as his own sons
They will serve their uncles in Canaan
They will stay behind in Pharaoh's house

cards.text: They're his, he says, just as Reuben and Simeon are his, and those are Jacob's two oldest sons (Genesis 29:32-33). The grandsons just got moved up a whole branch on the family tree!

cards.question: True or false: Jacob says any children Joseph has after these two will be counted as Jacob's too.

cards.text: Then Jacob remembers Rachel, his wife and Joseph's mother (Genesis 29:28; 30:22-24). On the way back from Paddan, to his sorrow, she died along the way in the land of Canaan.

cards.question: Rachel died along the way in Canaan. Where does Jacob bury her?

answers.text: In the cave with his fathers
Back in Paddan where they started

cards.text: Israel sees Joseph's sons and asks, "Who are these?" Joseph tells him they're the sons God has given him in this place.

cards.question: Jacob asks Joseph to bring the boys to him so he can bless them. True or false: Jacob can see Joseph's boys clearly when they come to him.

cards.text: Israel's eyesight is poor from old age, so poor he can hardly see. Joseph brings the boys close, and his father kisses and embraces them.

cards.question: Holding Joseph's boys, what does Israel tell Joseph?

answers.text: He never expected to see Joseph's face again and now sees his children too
He wishes Rachel had lived to see these two boys
He worried Joseph would never come back to visit him

cards.text: Then Joseph takes his sons off his father's knees and bows facedown. He lines them up with Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel's left, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel's right.

cards.question: Manasseh is Joseph's firstborn (Genesis 41:51-52), and he's lined up with Israel's right hand. What does Israel do?

answers.text: He crosses his hands and puts his right on Ephraim
He puts his right hand on Manasseh as lined up
He blesses Joseph and sends the boys outside

cards.text: He CROSSES his hands: right hand on Ephraim, the younger, left hand on Manasseh, the firstborn. Joseph lined those boys up like cookies on a tray, and Israel reached right across the tray.

Then he blesses Joseph and calls on the God before whom his grandfather Abraham and his father Isaac walked (Genesis 25:19-26), the God who has been his shepherd all his life, the angel who has redeemed him from all harm.

cards.question: Israel asks God to bless the boys and let them grow into a ___ upon the earth.
True or false: Israel asks that the boys be called by his name and the names of Abraham and Isaac.

cards.text: But Joseph sees his father's right hand on Ephraim's head, and he is displeased. He takes his father's hand to move it over to Manasseh's head, like a man straightening a crooked picture frame in somebody else's house.

cards.question: As Joseph moves his father's hand, what does he tell him?

answers.text: This one is the firstborn so put your right hand on him
Your eyes are tired so let me guide your hands
Ephraim is too young so bless him another day

cards.question: True or false: Israel lets Joseph move his right hand over to Manasseh.

cards.text: His father refuses: "I know, my son, I know!" Not one "I know," friend, TWO, and that's a man who knows EXACTLY where his hands are.

cards.question: Israel says Manasseh will become a people and be great too. So what does he say about Ephraim, the younger brother?

answers.text: He'll be greater and become a multitude of nations
He'll serve Manasseh for the rest of his life
He'll lead the whole family back to Canaan

cards.text: So that day Jacob blesses them, and he says that by them Israel will pronounce a blessing: may God make you like these two. Talk about getting your name written into the family cookie recipe.

cards.question: In the way Jacob blesses them, he puts ___ before ___.
Israel tells Joseph he's about to die. True or false: he also says God will be with Joseph and bring him back to the land of his fathers.
Last, Israel gives Joseph, as one above his brothers, something he took with his sword and bow from the Amorites, a people of Canaan (Genesis 10:15-16). What is it?

cards.text: We'll let this batch cool right here, friend. This family's story keeps on going.

findings.problem: Joseph first appears here as just a name in "Jacob, Joseph's father." The card never says who Joseph is. Jacob, Rachel, Reuben, Simeon, Abraham, Isaac and the Amorites all get a short introduction.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "Jacob has Joseph put his hand under his thigh and promise..." tells the hand and the promise as things Joseph has done. Genesis 47:29 only records Jacob's request. Joseph's answer and his oath come later (47:30-31). The question should say Jacob asks Joseph to do this.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "Now Jacob turns to Joseph's two boys" suggests Jacob looks at or speaks to the boys. In Genesis 48:5 he is talking to Joseph about them. In 48:8 he sees them and asks "Who are these?", so the text shows he hadn't turned to them yet. The card should say Jacob turns to the subject of Joseph's two boys.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He worried Joseph would never come back to visit him" is close in meaning to the right answer, "He never expected to see Joseph's face again." Both say Jacob thought he would not see Joseph again, so a baker could argue for it.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The right answer is much longer than the two wrong answers. Its length makes it stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Most of this card repeats the answer just given on card 6, which already said Israel crosses his hands and puts his right hand on Ephraim. Card 6 had also already called Manasseh the firstborn. The card adds almost nothing new besides the joke.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: "calls on the God..." turns Israel's blessing into a prayer. Genesis 48:15 says he blessed Joseph and said, "May the God..."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: "Israel asks God to bless the boys" is the same reframing as the doc's Ruth 1:8 example. Genesis 48:15-16 is a blessing spoken over Joseph and the boys ("may He bless these boys"), not a request to God.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: "Israel asks that the boys be called by his name..." frames the blessing line "may they be called by my name" (Genesis 48:16) as a request.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: "As Joseph moves his father's hand" says the hand actually moves. Genesis 48:17 says Joseph took the hand "to move it." Then 48:19-20 shows his father refused and kept his right hand on Ephraim. The card also blurs the answer the baker is asked for on card 13.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the "story isn't over" line, which the doc allows. It tells no verse but cites Genesis 48:22. The rule says a story card cites exactly the verses it tells.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the "story isn't over" line and tells no verse, what should its "verses" field cite: the passage's last verse, the stop's range, or something else?
